query: TPR's (Tapestry, Inc.) gift card liability breakage impact on revenue/prof profitability amid changing redemption patterns.
final_answer: Tapestry, Inc. (TPR) accounts for gift cards by recording the proceeds from their sale as a liability until the cards are redeemed by customers. Over time, TPR uses historical information to estimate the portion of gift card balances that will never be redeemed, a phenomenon known as "breakage." This estimated breakage is recognized as revenue over time, in proportion to actual customer redemptions, provided the company does not have a legal obligation to remit unredeemed amounts to any jurisdiction as unclaimed property. The impact of gift card breakage on revenue and profitability is that it provides a source of revenue separate from actual sales—when breakage is recognized, it increases reported revenue and, since there are no corresponding costs of goods sold, it also positively impacts profitability. If redemption patterns change (for example, if more customers begin redeeming gift cards than in the past), the amount of revenue recognized from breakage would decrease because a smaller portion of gift cards would be expected to go unredeemed. Conversely, if fewer gift cards are redeemed than historically, breakage revenue would increase. Thus, changing redemption patterns directly affect both revenue and profitability associated with gift card breakage. In summary, Tapestry's recognition of gift card breakage as revenue can enhance profitability, but this impact is sensitive to shifts in customer redemption patterns—greater redemptions reduce breakage revenue and profitability, while lower redemptions increase them.
